---
title: "Lettin Start + Void migration status"
description: "Current Lettin runtime and the work required before a native Worker cutover."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers
---

Lettin (`apps/lettin`) remains a Next.js app using OpenNext Cloudflare scripts.
It is not cut over tonight. Its Wrangler config names the existing
`tuturuuu-lettin` Worker, custom domain `lettin.tuturuuu.com`, D1 binding
`LETTIN_DB`, R2 bindings `LETTIN_MEDIA` and `NEXT_INC_CACHE_R2_BUCKET`,
`WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE`, and `ASSETS`. Runtime secret names are
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, and
`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`.

The current scripts build and deploy through OpenNext (`build:cloudflare`,
`deploy:cloudflare`, and `preview:cloudflare`). A native migration requires
porting the app routes and server behavior to TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void;
integrating the start-bridge boundary and request identity; replacing the
OpenNext-specific Worker and cache configuration with a native Worker profile;
preserving D1/R2 usage and auth behavior; and adding emitted-Worker runtime
fixtures, artifact acceptance, build-info smoke coverage and a cutover packet.
The existing database migrations are not part of that work and must not be run
as part of a source migration.

No native cutover or route change is authorized by this status page. A future
cutover needs a separately reviewed native artifact, staging acceptance,
release approval and an immutable Vercel deployment ID captured by Rex. Rollback
must restore the prior Vercel route without touching Lettin data.
